templates.text: Folate and iron are diverted to the placenta, leaving minimal reserve for maternal stores.
Iodine is preferentially shunted to the fetal thyroid, limiting maternal availability.
Glucose supply is tightly prioritized to placental transfer, reducing maternal energy substrates.
Calcium is allocated to fetal skeletal mineralization, with maternal serum levels declining.
DHA is retained for neural membrane synthesis, leaving maternal tissues with reduced absorption.
Amino acids are routed to placental protein synthesis, diminishing maternal plasma reserves.
Iron is sequestered for fetal hemoglobin production, curbing maternal erythrocyte turnover.
Folate remethylation cycles are suppressed in maternal liver, favoring placental transfer.
Iodine uptake by maternal thyroid is downregulated, shunting tracer to the fetus.
Glucose is partitioned to fetal brain metabolism, constricting maternal glycogen storage.
Calcium efflux from maternal bone is accelerated, while placental transport remains elevated.
DHA incorporation into maternal adipose is limited, preserving supply for fetal neurogenesis.
Amino acids are withdrawn from maternal muscle, redirected toward placental growth signals.
Folate-binding proteins in maternal serum are saturated, reducing systemic folate availability.
Iron absorption is upregulated in the placenta, yet maternal ferritin levels fall.
Iodine is recycled less efficiently in maternal kidneys, conserving urinary loss for fetal use.
Glucose uptake is enhanced in the placenta, lowering maternal blood glucose by {delta} mg/dL.
Calcium is mobilized from maternal bone stores, while placental transport rate remains high.
DHA is cleared from maternal plasma rapidly, favoring fetal accretion over maternal reserves.
Amino acid transporters are upregulated in the placenta, depleting maternal circulating pools.
Folate is preferentially methylated in the placenta, limiting maternal one-carbon metabolism.
Iron is redistributed from maternal bone marrow to placental transferrin receptors.
Iodine organification in maternal thyroid is suppressed, enhancing fetal thyroxine production.
Glucose is directed toward anaerobic glycolysis in the placenta, reducing maternal lactate clearance.
Calcium is shunted from maternal urine reabsorption, increasing fetal ionized calcium levels.
DHA is stored in maternal liver only after fetal needs are met, leaving a narrow margin.
Amino acids are diverted from maternal gluconeogenesis, supporting fetal protein deposition.
Folate is trapped in placental tissue as polyglutamates, lowering maternal serum folate.
Iron is preferentially loaded onto fetal hemoglobin, reducing maternal transferrin saturation.
Iodine flux across the placenta is unidirectional, conserving maternal stores only after delivery.
